selection_rationale: CPU-only NEURON+pymoo NSGA-II workload (3 sequential GA seeds at pop=96, N_EVAL=4, gens=20). Plan target: AMD EPYC 7B13 64-core CPU at Norway $0.24/hr; plan hourly cap: $0.40/hr (reject more expensive offers). Search at 2026-05-12T21:48:56Z: (1) Norway-only search returned 0 EPYC 7B13 offers; (2) global EPYC 7B13 64-effective-cores search returned one offer at $0.4690 (Spain, id=36368078, t0102's exact machine_id 11541) -- rejected by the $0.40/hr cap; (3) global EPYC>=32-cores dph<=0.55 search returned 15 EPYC offers. Three qualify under the cap or near it: Taiwan id=36157135 EPYC 7J13 128 eff-cores 125 GB RAM $0.3481 reliability 0.9993; Texas id=36639442 EPYC 7B13 43 eff-cores 331 GB RAM $0.4014 (technically $0.0014 over cap, with 33% reduced effective parallelism vs 7B13 64-core spec); Italy id=36605326 EPYC 7R32 48 eff-cores 125 GB RAM $0.2494 (older Rome arch, lower priority). SELECTED Taiwan id=36157135 (EPYC 7J13) on these grounds: (a) cheapest under-cap offer at $0.3481/hr -- 14% below the $0.40 cap, leaving runtime headroom for NEURON memory-leak slowdown buffer; (b) EPYC 7J13 is equivalent Zen 3 Milan silicon to the 7B13 (Google Cloud rebrand vs AWS rebrand of the same EPYC 7763), satisfying the plan's 'AMD EPYC 7B13 or equivalent' clause; (c) 128 effective cores at 2x t0102's 64-core baseline -- the actual pool size is min(60, cpu_count()-4) so all useful core slots will be filled; (d) reliability 0.9993 exceeds the 5-24h spec threshold of 0.995; (e) duration 35.5 days >> 40h runtime ceiling; (f) cuda_max_good 12.9 sufficient for the (unused) GPU sidecar. Compared offers explicitly rejected: Spain 36368078 EPYC 7B13 64-core $0.4690 (over $0.40 cap by $0.07/hr; was t0102's machine but the cap is a hard policy override); Texas 36639442 EPYC 7B13 43-eff-cores $0.4014 (over cap by $0.0014, and 43 vs 64 effective cores would push per-generation wall-clock by ~50%, eroding cost savings); NC 35550255 Xeon Gold 6140 $0.4006 (not EPYC, dropped). Estimated total cost at $0.3481/hr * 30 h plan productive estimate = ~$10.44; plus ~1h provisioning + smoke gate = ~$0.35; plus ~$0.05 idle teardown margin = ~$10.84 total expected, well under the $15 hard per-task cap. 125 GB RAM is below the plan's 200 GB target but matches t0102's actual usage on the Spain 125 GB machine which ran successfully; the in-process worker cache size is bounded by pop=96 * morphology-hash cache so peak working set is well under 60 GB observed in t0102.
